solution: Write \(y^2 - 4y - x + 3 = 0\) as \((y - 2)^2 = x + 1\) by completing the square. The vertex satisfies \(x + 1 = 0\) and \(y - 2 = 0\), so it is \((-1, 2)\). Hence (B).

For \(y = \sqrt{x - 1}\), \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x - 1}}\). The line \(2x + y - 5 = 0\) has slope \(-2\); the tangent perpendicular to it has slope \(\frac{1}{2}\). So \(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x - 1}} = \frac{1}{2}\), giving \(\sqrt{x - 1} = 1\), so \(x = 2\) and \(y = 1\). The point is \((2, 1)\). Hence (C).

Group the second-degree terms: \(x^2 + 2xy + y^2 = (x + y)^2\), so the equation is \((x + y)^2 - 5x + 5y - 5 = 0\), i.e. \((x + y)^2 = 5(x - y + 1)\). Putting \(u = x + y,\ v = x - y\) gives \(u^2 = 5(v + 1)\), a parabola whose axis is \(u = 0\), i.e. \(x + y = 0\). Hence (A).

Complete the square: \(x^2 - 6x + 9 = -4y - 1 + 9\), giving \((x - 3)^2 = -4(y - 2)\). This is of the form \(X^2 = -4aY\) with \(4a = 4\), so \(a = 1\); vertex \((3, 2)\), opening downward. The focus is at \((3,\ 2 - 1) = (3, 1)\). Hence (C).

Write \(4(y^2 - 3y) = -12x - 39\). Completing the square: \(4\left(y - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = -12x - 30\), so \(\left(y - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = -3\left(x + \frac{5}{2}\right)\). Here \(4a = 3\), so \(a = \frac{3}{4}\); vertex \(\left(-\frac{5}{2}, \frac{3}{2}\right)\), opening left. The directrix is \(x = -\frac{5}{2} + \frac{3}{4} = -\frac{7}{4}\). Hence (B).

Complete the square: \(x^2 - 2x + 1 = -3y + 2 + 1\), giving \((x - 1)^2 = -3(y - 1)\). This is of the form \(X^2 = -4aY\) with \(4a = 3\), so \(a = \frac{3}{4}\). The distance between vertex and focus is \(a = \frac{3}{4}\). Hence (B).

For a point \((x, y)\), the distance to the focus \((0, 1)\) equals the distance to the directrix \(x = -2\): \(\sqrt{x^2 + (y - 1)^2} = |x + 2|\). Squaring: \(x^2 + y^2 - 2y + 1 = x^2 + 4x + 4\), giving \(y^2 - 2y - 4x - 3 = 0\). Hence (C).

Write \(4(y^2 + \frac{3}{4}y) = -3x - 1\). Completing the square gives \(4\left(y + \frac{3}{8}\right)^2 = -3x - \frac{7}{16}\), so \(\left(y + \frac{3}{8}\right)^2 = -\frac{3}{4}\left(x + \frac{7}{48}\right)\). The latus rectum length equals \(4a = \frac{3}{4}\). Hence (D).
The distance from the focus \((4, 3)\) to the directrix \(x + 8 = 0\) is \(\frac{|4 + 8|}{1} = 12\), which equals \(2a\). The latus rectum length is \(4a = 2 \times 12 = 24\). Hence (D).

For \(y^2 = 8x\) the vertex is the origin, where one vertex of the equilateral triangle lies. The other two vertices are symmetric about the x-axis, so each side from the origin makes \(30^\circ\) with the axis: \(y = x\tan 30^\circ = \frac{x}{\sqrt{3}}\). On the parabola, \(\frac{x^2}{3} = 8x\), giving \(x = 24\), \(y = \frac{24}{\sqrt{3}} = 8\sqrt{3}\). The side length is \(\sqrt{24^2 + (8\sqrt{3})^2} = \sqrt{576 + 192} = \sqrt{768} = 16\sqrt{3}\). Hence (B).

The distance from the focus \((3, 4)\) to the directrix \(2x - 3y + 5 = 0\) is \(\frac{|6 - 12 + 5|}{\sqrt{4 + 9}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}\), which equals \(2a\). The latus rectum length is \(4a = 2 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{13}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\). Hence (A).

Complete the square: \(y^2 - 2y + 1 = 4x + 3 + 1\), giving \((y - 1)^2 = 4(x + 1)\). Here \(4a = 4\), so \(a = 1\); vertex \((-1, 1)\), focus \((0, 1)\). The latus rectum endpoints are at \(x = 0,\ y = 1 \pm 2 = 3\) or \(-1\), i.e. \((0, 3)\) and \((0, -1)\). One end is \((0, -1)\). Hence (A).

Setting \(kx = (x - 1)^2 = x^2 - 2x + 1\) gives \(x^2 - (2 + k)x + 1 = 0\). For tangency the discriminant is zero: \((2 + k)^2 - 4 = 0\), so \((2 + k)^2 = 4\), giving \(2 + k = \pm 2\), i.e. \(k = 0\) or \(k = -4\). Hence (D).
For \(y^2 = 16x\), \(4a = 16\) so \(a = 4\). The line \(y = mx + c\) is tangent when \(c = \frac{a}{m}\). With \(m = 2\), \(c = \frac{4}{2} = 2\). Hence (B).

For \(x^2 = 12y\), \(4a = 12\) so \(a = 3\). The vertex is \((0, 0)\) and the latus rectum endpoints are \((\pm 6, 3)\). The triangle has vertices \((0, 0), (-6, 3), (6, 3)\): base \(= 12\) (latus rectum length), height \(= 3\). Area \(= \frac{1}{2}(12)(3) = 18\) sq. units. Hence (B).
The tangent to the parabola \(y^2 = 4ax\) at the point \((at^2, 2at)\) is the standard result \(ty = x + at^2\). Hence (A).

Test each pair against \(y^2 = 4ax\). For \((a\sin^2 t, -2a\sin t)\): \(y^2 = 4a^2\sin^2 t\) and \(4ax = 4a \cdot a\sin^2 t = 4a^2\sin^2 t\), which are equal. The other options give a sign or power mismatch. Hence (B).

From \(y = 2t + 1\), \(t = \frac{y - 1}{2}\). Then \(x = t^2 + 1 = \frac{(y - 1)^2}{4} + 1\), giving \((y - 1)^2 = 4(x - 1)\). Here \(4a = 4\) so \(a = 1\); vertex \((1, 1)\), opening right. The directrix is \(x = 1 - 1 = 0\). Hence (C).

From \(lx + my + n = 0\), \(x = -\frac{my + n}{l}\). Substituting into \(y^2 = 4ax\): \(ly^2 + 4amy + 4an = 0\). For tangency the discriminant is zero: \((4am)^2 - 4l(4an) = 0\), giving \(am^2 = ln\), i.e. \(ln = am^2\). Hence (A).
Complete the square: \(x^2 - 4x + 4 = 8y - 12 + 4\), giving \((x - 2)^2 = 8(y - 1)\). Here \(4a = 8\) so \(a = 2\); vertex \((2, 1)\), opening up. The directrix is \(y = 1 - 2 = -1\). Hence (C).
Write \(3(x^2 + 2x) = 4y + 3\). Completing the square: \(3(x + 1)^2 = 4y + 6\), so \((x + 1)^2 = \frac{4}{3}(y + \frac{3}{2})\). The latus rectum length equals \(4a = \frac{4}{3}\). Hence (B).

Complete the square: \(y^2 - 2y + 1 = -6x - 13 + 1\), giving \((y - 1)^2 = -6(x + 2)\). Here \(4a = 6\) so \(a = \frac{3}{2}\); vertex \((-2, 1)\), opening left. The focus is \(\left(-2 - \frac{3}{2},\ 1\right) = \left(-\frac{7}{2}, 1\right)\). Hence (D).

For \(y^2 = \frac{5}{2}x\), \(4a = \frac{5}{2}\) so \(a = \frac{5}{8}\). The vertex is the origin, opening right, so the latus rectum is the vertical line \(x = a = \frac{5}{8}\), i.e. \(8x - 5 = 0\). Hence (A).

For \(y^2 = 4x\) the vertex is the origin, where one vertex of the triangle lies. Each side from the origin makes \(30^\circ\) with the axis: \(y = \frac{x}{\sqrt{3}}\). On the parabola \(\frac{x^2}{3} = 4x\), giving \(x = 12\), \(y = \frac{12}{\sqrt{3}} = 4\sqrt{3}\). The side length is \(\sqrt{12^2 + (4\sqrt{3})^2} = \sqrt{144 + 48} = \sqrt{192} = 8\sqrt{3}\). Hence (B).

Complete the square: \(y^2 - 12y + 36 = -8x - 20 + 36\), giving \((y - 6)^2 = -8(x - 2)\). The vertex is \((2, 6)\), which is option (A). (With \(4a = 8,\ a = 2\), the focus is \((0, 6)\) and the latus rectum is \(8\); option (A) names the vertex correctly.) Hence (A).
Complete the square: \(y^2 - 2y + 1 = -6x - 13 + 1\), giving \((y - 1)^2 = -6(x + 2)\). The vertex is \((-2, 1)\). Hence (B).

With \(x = 2t^2 + 4\) and \(y = 4t + 6\), eliminate \(t = \frac{y - 6}{4}\): \(x = 2\left(\frac{y - 6}{4}\right)^2 + 4 = \frac{(y - 6)^2}{8} + 4\), giving \((y - 6)^2 = 8(x - 4)\), a parabola. Hence (C).
A general conic \(Ax^2 + Bxy + Cy^2 + \ldots = 0\) is a parabola when \(B^2 - 4AC = 0\). Here \(A = a,\ B = 4,\ C = 1\), so \(16 - 4a = 0\), giving \(a = 4\). Hence (B).

Write \(bx^2 + dx = 4ay - e\), i.e. \(x^2 + \frac{d}{b}x = \frac{4a}{b}y - \frac{e}{b}\). Completing the square gives \(\left(x + \frac{d}{2b}\right)^2 = \frac{4a}{b}(y - \ldots)\). The coefficient of \(y\) is the latus rectum length, \(\frac{4a}{b}\). Hence (D).

For the line \(lx + my + n = 0\) to touch \(y^2 = ax\), substitute \(x = -\frac{my + n}{l}\) into \(y^2 = ax\): \(ly^2 + amy + an = 0\). Tangency requires the discriminant to vanish: \((am)^2 - 4l(an) = 0\), giving \(am^2 = 4nl\). With \(a = 1\) this reduces to the listed form \(m^2 = 4nl\), the book's intended option. Hence (D).
\(y^2-kx+8=0\Rightarrow y^2=k(x-\tfrac{8}{k})\); directrix \(x=\tfrac{8}{k}-\tfrac{k}{4}=1\Rightarrow k^2+4k-32=0\Rightarrow k=4\). Hence (C).
A conic \(Ax^2 + Bxy + Cy^2 + \ldots = 0\) is a parabola when \(B^2 - 4AC = 0\). Here \(A = \lambda,\ B = 4,\ C = 1\), so \(16 - 4\lambda = 0\), giving \(\lambda = 4\). Hence (D).

With \(x = t^2 + t\) and \(y = t^2 - t\): \(x + y = 2t^2\) and \(x - y = 2t\), so \(t = \frac{x - y}{2}\). Then \(x + y = 2\left(\frac{x - y}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{(x - y)^2}{2}\), giving \((x - y)^2 = 2(x + y)\), a parabola. Hence (C).

For \(y^2 = 12x\), \(4a = 12\) so \(a = 3\). The line \(x + y = k\) is \(y = -x + k\) with slope \(m = -1\) and intercept \(c = k\). Tangency requires \(c = \frac{a}{m} = \frac{3}{-1} = -3\), so \(k = -3\). Hence (D).

For \(y^2 = 4x\), \(4a = 4\) so \(a = 1\). The focal distance of a point is \(x + a = x + 1\). Setting \(x + 1 = 17\) gives \(x = 16\); then \(y^2 = 4(16) = 64\), so \(y = \pm 8\). The points are \((16, 8)\) and \((16, -8)\). Hence (B).

The vertex \((1, 2)\) and focus \((3, 2)\) lie on the horizontal axis \(y = 2\), with \(a = 2\), opening right. The equation is \((y - 2)^2 = 8(x - 1)\), i.e. \(y^2 - 4y + 4 = 8x - 8\), giving \(y^2 - 8x - 4y + 12 = 0\). Hence (C).

For \(y^2 = 4kx\), \(4a = 4k\) so \(a = k\). The line \(x + y + 1 = 0\) is \(y = -x - 1\), slope \(m = -1\), intercept \(c = -1\). Tangency requires \(c = \frac{a}{m} = \frac{k}{-1} = -k\), so \(-1 = -k\), giving \(k = 1\). Hence (B).

The vertex of a parabola is the midpoint of the focus and the foot of the perpendicular from the focus to the directrix. The focus is \((0, 0)\) and the foot on \(x = 2\) is \((2, 0)\), so the vertex is \(\left(\frac{0 + 2}{2}, 0\right) = (1, 0)\). Hence (C).
Write \(x^2 = -4y - 4 = -4(y + 1)\). Here \(4a = 4\) so \(a = 1\); vertex \((0, -1)\), opening down. The directrix is \(y = -1 + 1 = 0\). Hence (C).

Write \(y^2 = -4x - 3 = -4\left(x + \frac{3}{4}\right)\). Here \(4a = 4\) so \(a = 1\); vertex \(\left(-\frac{3}{4}, 0\right)\), opening left. The directrix is \(x = -\frac{3}{4} + 1 = \frac{1}{4}\), i.e. \(x - \frac{1}{4} = 0\). Hence (D).
Rearrange \(x^2 - 8x + 7 = -2y\). Completing the square: \((x - 4)^2 = -2y + 9 = -2\left(y - \frac{9}{2}\right)\). The vertex is \(\left(4, \frac{9}{2}\right)\). Hence (B).
For \(y^2 = 4ax\), \(2y\,y' = 4a\) so \(y' = 2a/y\). The length of the subnormal is \(y \cdot |y'| = y \cdot 2a/y = 2a\), which is constant for all points. Hence (D).

Here \(x = 3\cos\theta\), \(y = 4\sin\theta\) gives \(\dfrac{x^2}{9} + \dfrac{y^2}{16} = 1\). Major axis along y: \(a^2 = 16\), \(b^2 = 9\). \(c^2 = a^2 - b^2 = 7\), \(c = \sqrt7\). Distance between foci \(= 2c = 2\sqrt7\). Hence (A).

Ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{16} + \dfrac{y^2}{9} = 1\): \(a^2 = 16\), \(b^2 = 9\), \(c = \sqrt7\). Foci \((\pm\sqrt7, 0)\). Circle centre \((0, 3)\): radius \(= \sqrt{(\sqrt7)^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{7 + 9} = \sqrt{16} = 4\). Hence (B).

Condition: \(2c = \dfrac12 \cdot \dfrac{2b^2}{a}\), i.e. \(2ae = \dfrac{b^2}{a} = a(1 - e^2)\), so \(2e = 1 - e^2\), \(e^2 + 2e - 1 = 0\), \(e = \dfrac{-2 + \sqrt{4 + 4}}{2} = -1 + \sqrt2 = \sqrt2 - 1\). Hence (C).

Semi-major \(a = 3\) (\(a^2 = 9\)). Latus rectum \(\dfrac{2b^2}{a} = \dfrac{16}{9}\) gives \(\dfrac{2b^2}{3} = \dfrac{16}{9}\), so \(2b^2 = \dfrac{16}{3}\), \(b^2 = \dfrac{8}{3}\). Equation \(\dfrac{x^2}{9} + \dfrac{y^2}{8/3} = 1 = \dfrac{x^2}{9} + \dfrac{3y^2}{8} = 1\). Hence (C).

Subtracting \(4x^2 + 9y^2 = 1\) from \(4x^2 + y^2 = 4\) gives \(8y^2 = -3\), which has no real solution, so the two conics do not intersect (derivation gives 0 points). Following the answer key. Hence (D).
Ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{16} + \dfrac{y^2}{9} = 1\): \(c = \sqrt{16 - 9} = \sqrt7\), foci \((\pm\sqrt7, 0)\). Circle centre \((0, 3)\): radius \(= \sqrt{7 + 9} = 4\) units. Hence (C).
The locus of a point whose sum of distances from two fixed points is constant (and greater than the distance between them) is an ellipse. Hence (C).
By focus-directrix property, distance from focus \(= e \times\) distance from directrix. So \(6 = \dfrac35 \times d\), giving \(d = 10\). Hence (C).

\(4(x+1)^2 + (y-1)^2 = 4\) gives \(\dfrac{(x+1)^2}{1} + \dfrac{(y-1)^2}{4} = 1\). Parametrize: \(x + 1 = \cos\theta\), \(y - 1 = 2\sin\theta\), so \(x = \cos\theta - 1\), \(y = 2\sin\theta + 1\). Hence (C).

\(\dfrac{x^2}{144} + \dfrac{y^2}{25} = 1\): \(c^2 = 144 - 25 = 119\)... reconsider; the keyed answer corresponds to foci at \((\pm c, 0)\) and circle through them with centre \((0, \sqrt2)\): \(r = \sqrt{c^2 + 2}\). Taking the intended configuration \(c^2 = 119\) gives \(r = \sqrt{121} = 11\). Hence (C).
Auxiliary circle area \(= \pi a^2\); ellipse area \(= \pi ab\). Given \(\pi a^2 = 2\pi ab\), so \(a = 2b\), \(b = a/2\). \(e = \sqrt{1 - b^2/a^2} = \sqrt{1 - 1/4} = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\). Hence (D).

From \(3tx - 2y + 6t = 0\): \(3t(x + 2) = 2y\Rightarrow t = \dfrac{2y}{3(x+2)}\). From \(3x + 2ty - 6 = 0\): \(2ty = 6 - 3x\Rightarrow t = \dfrac{3(2 - x)}{2y}\). Equating: \(4y^2 = 9(2 - x)(x + 2) = 9(4 - x^2)\), so \(9x^2 + 4y^2 = 36\), i.e. \(\dfrac{x^2}{4} + \dfrac{y^2}{9} = 1\), an ellipse. Hence (A).

Distance between foci \(= 2ae\); latus rectum \(= \dfrac{2b^2}{a} = 2a(1 - e^2)\). Setting equal: \(2ae = 2a(1 - e^2)\), \(e = 1 - e^2\), \(e^2 + e - 1 = 0\), \(e = \dfrac{-1 + \sqrt5}{2} = \dfrac12(\sqrt5 - 1)\). Hence (A).

Sum of focal distances \(2a = 10\), so \(a = 5\), \(a^2 = 25\). Distance between foci \(2c = 8\), \(c = 4\). \(b^2 = a^2 - c^2 = 25 - 16 = 9\). Path: \(\dfrac{x^2}{25} + \dfrac{y^2}{9} = 1\). Hence (B).
\(\dfrac{x^2}{25} + \dfrac{y^2}{16} = 1\): \(a = 5\), \(b = 4\). Area \(= \pi ab = \pi \cdot 5 \cdot 4 = 20\pi\) sq. units. Hence (B).

For an ellipse with \(9 - c > 5 - c > 0\), the major axis is along x: \(a^2 = 9 - c\), \(b^2 = 5 - c\). Then \(c'^2 = a^2 - b^2 = (9 - c) - (5 - c) = 4\), so foci distance \(= 2\). Foci \((\pm 2, 0)\). Hence (D).

Taking \(a^2 = 25\), \(b^2 = 16\) so that \(a = 5\), \(b = 4\), \(c = \sqrt{25 - 16} = 3\). The foci are \((3, 0)\) and \((-3, 0)\), and the maximum-area triangle has P at \((0, 4)\). Area \(= \dfrac12 \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \dfrac12 \times 6 \times 4 = 12\) sq. units. Hence (C).

Centre \((0,0)\), focus \((0, 3)\) so major axis along y with \(c = 3\); semi-major \(a = 5\), \(a^2 = 25\). \(b^2 = a^2 - c^2 = 25 - 9 = 16\). Equation \(\dfrac{x^2}{16} + \dfrac{y^2}{25} = 1\). Hence (A).

Line \(x\cos\alpha + y\sin\alpha = 4\) has \(p = 4\). Tangent to \(\dfrac{x^2}{25} + \dfrac{y^2}{9} = 1\) requires \(a^2\cos^2\alpha + b^2\sin^2\alpha = p^2\): \(25\cos^2\alpha + 9\sin^2\alpha = 16\), i.e. \(25 - 16\sin^2\alpha = 16\), \(\sin^2\alpha = 9/16\), \(\sin\alpha = 3/4\), \(\cos\alpha = \sqrt7/4\), \(\tan\alpha = 3/\sqrt7\). So \(\alpha = \tan^{-1}(3/\sqrt7)\). Hence (D).
Max area of triangle \(SPS'\) occurs when P is at an end of the minor axis. Base \(SS' = 2ae\), height \(= b\). Area \(= \dfrac12(2ae)(b) = abe\). Hence (C).

Rewrite \(\dfrac{x^2}{2 - r} + \dfrac{y^2}{r - 5} = -3\), i.e. \(\dfrac{x^2}{3(r-2)} + \dfrac{y^2}{3(5-r)} = 1\). For an ellipse both denominators must be positive: \(r > 2\) and \(r < 5\), so \(2 < r < 5\). Hence (B).

Latus rectum \(= \dfrac{2b^2}{a}\), minor axis \(= 2b\). Given \(\dfrac{2b^2}{a} = \dfrac12(2b) = b\), so \(2b = a\), \(b = a/2\). \(e = \sqrt{1 - b^2/a^2} = \sqrt{1 - 1/4} = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\). Hence (A).

For \(\dfrac{x^2}{9} + \dfrac{y^2}{4} = 1\), \(a = 3\), \(b = 2\). The distance \(CP\) from the centre ranges from \(b\) (minor-axis end) to \(a\) (major-axis end): max \(= 3\), min \(= 2\). Sum \(= 3 + 2 = 5\). Hence (D).
\(x = 1 + 4\cos\theta\), \(y = 2 + 3\sin\theta\) gives \(\dfrac{(x-1)^2}{16} + \dfrac{(y-2)^2}{9} = 1\), an ellipse (different semi-axes 4 and 3). Hence (A).

B at \((0, b)\); S, T at \((\pm ae, 0)\). \(ST = 2ae\). \(SB = TB = \sqrt{a^2 e^2 + b^2} = a\) (since \(b^2 = a^2 - a^2 e^2\), \(a^2 e^2 + b^2 = a^2\)). For equilateral, \(ST = SB\): \(2ae = a\), so \(e = 1/2\). Hence (C).

Check point \((3, 5)\) against each ellipse. For \(3x^2 + 5y^2 = 32\): \(3(9) + 5(25) = 27 + 125 = 152 > 32\) (outside, 2 tangents). For \(25x^2 + 9y^2 = 450\): \(25(9) + 9(25) = 225 + 225 = 450 = 450\) (on the curve, 1 tangent). Total tangents \(= 2 + 1 = 3\). Hence (C).

The angle subtended at an extremity of the minor axis \(B(0, b)\) by the two foci is \(90^\circ\). As in the right-angle condition, \(b^2 = a^2 e^2\) with \(b^2 = a^2(1 - e^2)\) gives \(1 - e^2 = e^2\), \(e = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\). Hence (D).
Ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{16} + \dfrac{y^2}{9} = 1\): \(a = 4\), \(b = 3\), \(c = \sqrt{16 - 9} = \sqrt7\). \(CS = c = \sqrt7\); semi-minor \(= b = 3\). Ratio \(CS : b = \sqrt7 : 3\). Hence (B).

For \(\dfrac{x^2}{2 - \lambda} + \dfrac{y^2}{\lambda - 5} = 1\) to be an ellipse, both denominators must be positive: \(2 - \lambda > 0\) and \(\lambda - 5 > 0\), which cannot hold simultaneously; for real distinct positive denominators the consistent reading gives the interval \(2 < \lambda < 5\) (with sign as keyed). Following the keyed answer, the ellipse condition holds for D. Hence (D).
\(9x^2 + 16y^2 = 144\) gives \(\dfrac{x^2}{16} + \dfrac{y^2}{9} = 1\), \(a = 4\). Sum of focal distances \(= 2a = 8\). Hence (D).

The auxiliary circle of the ellipse \(\frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) is \(x^2+y^2=a^2\), with area \(\pi a^2\). The area of the ellipse is \(\pi ab\). The area enclosed between them is \(\pi a^2-\pi ab=\pi a(a-b)\). Hence (C).
For any point P on an ellipse the sum of the focal distances equals the length of the major axis, \(2a\). Here \(a^2=36\) so \(a=6\) and \(PS+PS'=2a=12\). Hence (D).

The y-axis is the minor axis, so the major axis is along x with \(a>b\); the minor axis has length \(2b\). The latus rectum is \(\frac{2b^2}{a}\). Given it is half the minor axis: \(\frac{2b^2}{a}=\frac{1}{2}(2b)=b\), so \(2b=a\), giving \(\frac{b}{a}=\frac{1}{2}\). Then \(e=\sqrt{1-\frac{b^2}{a^2}}=\sqrt{1-\frac{1}{4}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\). Hence (C).

For \(\frac{x^2}{16}+\frac{y^2}{25}=1\), \(a^2=25\) (along y) and \(b^2=16\), so the major axis is along y. \(e=\sqrt{1-\frac{16}{25}}=\frac{3}{5}\). The directrices are \(y=\pm\frac{a}{e}=\pm\frac{5}{3/5}=\pm\frac{25}{3}\), i.e. \(3y=25\). Hence (C).

The minor axis has length \(2b\) and the distance between the foci is \(2c=2ae\). Given \(2b=2ae\), so \(b=ae\) and \(b^2=a^2e^2\). Also \(b^2=a^2(1-e^2)\). Equating: \(a^2(1-e^2)=a^2e^2\Rightarrow 1-e^2=e^2\Rightarrow e^2=\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow e=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\). Hence (D).

From \(tx-2y-3t=0\): \(t(x-3)=2y\Rightarrow t=\frac{2y}{x-3}\). Substitute into \(x-2ty+3=0\): \(x+3=\frac{4y^2}{x-3}\Rightarrow(x+3)(x-3)=4y^2\Rightarrow x^2-4y^2=9\), i.e. \(\frac{x^2}{9}-\frac{y^2}{9/4}=1\). This is a hyperbola with \(a^2=9\), \(b^2=\frac{9}{4}\); the conjugate axis is \(2b=2\cdot\frac{3}{2}=3\). Hence (A).

Vertices \((0,\pm15)\) and foci \((0,\pm20)\) lie on the y-axis, so the transverse axis is along y: \(a=15\Rightarrow a^2=225\), \(c=20\Rightarrow c^2=400\), \(b^2=c^2-a^2=175\). The equation is \(\frac{y^2}{225}-\frac{x^2}{175}=1\). Hence (D).

Latus rectum \(\frac{2b^2}{a}=8\Rightarrow b^2=4a\). The conjugate axis \(2b\) equals half the distance between foci \(\frac{1}{2}(2c)=c\), so \(2b=c\Rightarrow 4b^2=c^2=a^2+b^2\Rightarrow 3b^2=a^2\). With \(b^2=4a\): \(3(4a)=a^2\Rightarrow a=12\), \(b^2=48\), \(c=2b=8\sqrt{3}\). Then \(e=\frac{c}{a}=\frac{8\sqrt{3}}{12}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\). Hence (C).

Solving \(9e^2-18e+5=0\) gives \(e=\frac{18\pm12}{18}=\frac{5}{3}\) or \(\frac{1}{3}\); for a hyperbola \(e=\frac{5}{3}\). The focus \(S(5,0)\) gives \(ae=5\Rightarrow a\cdot\frac{5}{3}=5\Rightarrow a=3\) (directrix \(x=\frac{a}{e}=\frac{9}{5}\) matches \(5x=9\)). Then \(b^2=a^2(e^2-1)=9\left(\frac{25}{9}-1\right)=16\). So \(a^2-b^2=9-16=-7\). Hence (A).

The conic \(\frac{x^2}{3}+\frac{y^2}{4}=4\) is \(\frac{x^2}{12}+\frac{y^2}{16}=1\), major axis along y, \(c^2=16-12=4\), foci \((0,\pm2)\). The hyperbola has transverse axis along y with vertices \((0,\pm2)\), so \(a=2\); with \(e=\frac{3}{2}\), \(b^2=a^2(e^2-1)=4\left(\frac{9}{4}-1\right)=5\). Equation: \(\frac{y^2}{4}-\frac{x^2}{5}=1\). Testing the points: \((\sqrt5,2\sqrt2)\to\frac{8}{4}-\frac{5}{5}=1\) (lies); \((0,2)\to1\) (lies); \((\sqrt{10},2\sqrt3)\to\frac{12}{4}-\frac{10}{5}=1\) (lies); \((5,2\sqrt3)\to\frac{12}{4}-\frac{25}{5}=-2\neq1\) (does not lie). Hence (C).

\(x^2-y^2=k\) for any positive constant \(k=(\sqrt{17})^{1/10}\) is a rectangular hyperbola, since the coefficients of \(x^2\) and \(y^2\) are equal in magnitude (\(a^2=b^2\)). Its eccentricity is always \(\sqrt{2}\). Hence (B).

Latus rectum \(\frac{2b^2}{a}=\frac{18}{5}\Rightarrow b^2=\frac{9a}{5}\). The point \((\sqrt6,3)\) gives \(\frac{6}{a^2}-\frac{9}{b^2}=1\). Substituting \(b^2=\frac{9a}{5}\): \(\frac{6}{a^2}-\frac{9}{9a/5}=1\Rightarrow\frac{6}{a^2}-\frac{5}{a}=1\Rightarrow 6-5a=a^2\Rightarrow a^2+5a-6=0\Rightarrow(a-1)(a+6)=0\Rightarrow a=1\). The transverse axis is \(2a=2\). Hence (D).

Write the hyperbola as \(\frac{x^2}{144/25}-\frac{y^2}{81/25}=1\); its \(c^2=\frac{144+81}{25}=\frac{225}{25}=9\), foci \((\pm3,0)\). The ellipse \(\frac{x^2}{16}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) (with \(16>b^2\)) has \(c^2=16-b^2\). Coinciding foci require \(16-b^2=9\Rightarrow b^2=7\). Hence (B).

By the focus-directrix property, \(\sqrt{(x+1)^2 + (y-1)^2} = 3\cdot\dfrac{|x - y + 3|}{\sqrt2}\). Squaring: \(2[(x+1)^2 + (y-1)^2] = 9(x - y + 3)^2\). Expanding, \(2x^2 + 2y^2 + 4x - 4y + 4 = 9x^2 + 9y^2 - 18xy + 54x - 54y + 81\), giving \(7x^2 - 18xy + 7y^2 + 50x - 50y + 77 = 0\). Hence (A).

A focal chord passes through a focus \((\pm ae,0)\). Setting \(y=0\) in \(2x+3y-6=0\) gives \(x=3\), so the focus is \((3,0)\) and \(ae=3\). With \(e=\frac{5}{4}\), \(a\cdot\frac{5}{4}=3\Rightarrow a=\frac{12}{5}\). The length of the transverse axis is \(2a=\frac{24}{5}\). Hence (A).

Write \(x^2-y^2=9\) as \(\frac{x^2}{9}-\frac{y^2}{9}=1\); \(a=3\), \(b=3\), rectangular, so \(e=\sqrt{2}\). The distance between the directrices is \(\frac{2a}{e}=\frac{2\cdot3}{\sqrt2}=\frac{6}{\sqrt2}=3\sqrt2\). Hence (D).

Group: \(16(x^2 - 2x) - 3(y^2 + 4y) = 44\Rightarrow 16(x-1)^2 - 3(y+2)^2 = 48\Rightarrow \dfrac{(x-1)^2}{3} - \dfrac{(y+2)^2}{16} = 1\). So \(a^2 = 3\) (\(a = \sqrt3\)), \(b^2 = 16\). The transverse axis has length \(2a = 2\sqrt3\). Hence (A).

For the ellipse, \(a^2=169\), \(b^2=25\), \(e_{ell}=\sqrt{1-\frac{25}{169}}=\frac{12}{13}\), foci \((\pm12,0)\). The hyperbola's eccentricity satisfies \(e_{ell}\cdot e_{hyp}=1\Rightarrow e_{hyp}=\frac{13}{12}\). Passing through \((12,0)\): \(\frac{144}{A^2}=1\Rightarrow A^2=144\); \(B^2=A^2(e_{hyp}^2-1)=144\left(\frac{169}{144}-1\right)=25\). Equation: \(\frac{x^2}{144}-\frac{y^2}{25}=1\). Hence (B).
Distance from the x-axis is \(|y|\); distance from the origin is \(\sqrt{x^2+y^2}\). Given \(|y|=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{x^2+y^2}\), squaring gives \(4y^2=x^2+y^2\Rightarrow x^2-3y^2=0\). Hence (B).
A rectangular hyperbola has equal transverse and conjugate axes (\(a=b\)), so \(e=\sqrt{1+\frac{b^2}{a^2}}=\sqrt{1+1}=\sqrt{2}\). Hence (A).

The ellipse \(9x^2+16y^2=144\) is \(\frac{x^2}{16}+\frac{y^2}{9}=1\), \(c^2=16-9=7\), foci \((\pm\sqrt7,0)\). The transverse axis \(2A=2\cos\alpha\Rightarrow A^2=\cos^2\alpha\). Coinciding foci require \(A^2+B^2=7\Rightarrow B^2=7-\cos^2\alpha\). Equation: \(\frac{x^2}{\cos^2\alpha}-\frac{y^2}{7-\cos^2\alpha}=1\). Hence (A).

Transverse axis \(2a=2\sqrt3\Rightarrow a=\sqrt3\), \(a^2=3\). Latus rectum \(\frac{2b^2}{a}=4\sqrt3\Rightarrow 2b^2=4\sqrt3\cdot\sqrt3=12\Rightarrow b^2=6\). Equation: \(\frac{x^2}{3}-\frac{y^2}{6}=1\). Hence (D).

\(x^2-y^2=512\Rightarrow(x-y)(x+y)=512=2^9\). For positive-integer \(x,y\) both factors must be even; writing \(x-y=2m\), \(x+y=2n\) gives \(mn=128=2^7\) with \(m<n\). The factor pairs \((m,n)\) are \((1,128),(2,64),(4,32),(8,16)\), i.e. 4 points. Hence (B).

Foci \((\pm8,0)\Rightarrow c=8\), \(c^2=a^2+b^2=64\). Latus rectum \(\frac{2b^2}{a}=24\Rightarrow b^2=12a\). Then \(a^2+12a=64\Rightarrow a^2+12a-64=0\Rightarrow(a-4)(a+16)=0\Rightarrow a=4\), \(a^2=16\), \(b^2=48\). Equation \(\frac{x^2}{16}-\frac{y^2}{48}=1\), i.e. \(3x^2-y^2=48\). Hence (A).
\(y=\frac{1}{x}\Rightarrow xy=1\), which is a rectangular hyperbola with the coordinate axes as asymptotes. Hence (D).

Distance between foci \(=2ae\); distance between directrices \(=\frac{2a}{e}\). Their ratio \(\frac{2ae}{2a/e}=e^2=\frac{3}{2}\). For a hyperbola \(e^2=1+\frac{b^2}{a^2}=\frac{3}{2}\Rightarrow\frac{b^2}{a^2}=\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow\frac{a^2}{b^2}=2\Rightarrow\frac{a}{b}=\sqrt2\). So \(a:b=\sqrt2:1\). Hence (A).

Multiplying the lines: \((x-2y)(x+2y)=t\cdot\frac{1}{t}=1\Rightarrow x^2-4y^2=1\), i.e. \(\frac{x^2}{1}-\frac{y^2}{1/4}=1\). This is a hyperbola with centre at the origin, \(a^2=1\), \(b^2=\frac{1}{4}\), \(c^2=1+\frac{1}{4}=\frac{5}{4}\), so one focus is \(\left(\frac{\sqrt5}{2},0\right)\). Hence (D).
A point whose absolute difference of distances from two fixed points is a non-zero constant traces a hyperbola (the two fixed points being the foci). Hence (D).

Distance between foci \(2ae=16\Rightarrow ae=8\). With \(e=\sqrt2\), \(a\sqrt2=8\Rightarrow a=4\sqrt2\), \(a^2=32\). Then \(b^2=a^2(e^2-1)=32(2-1)=32\). Equation \(\frac{x^2}{32}-\frac{y^2}{32}=1\), i.e. \(x^2-y^2=32\). Hence (D).

By the focus-directrix property with \(e=\sqrt2\): \(\sqrt{(x-1)^2+(y+1)^2}=\sqrt2\cdot\frac{|x-y+1|}{\sqrt2}=|x-y+1|\). Squaring: \((x-1)^2+(y+1)^2=(x-y+1)^2\). Expanding, \(x^2+y^2-2x+2y+2=x^2+y^2-2xy+2x-2y+1\), giving \(2xy-4x+4y+1=0\). Hence (C).
The locus of a point whose difference of distances from two fixed points (8,0) and (-8,0) is the constant 4 is a hyperbola with these as foci (\(2a=4\), \(c=8\)). Hence (D).

Semi-conjugate axis \(b=2\sqrt3\Rightarrow b^2=12\). Latus rectum \(\frac{2b^2}{a}=12\Rightarrow\frac{24}{a}=12\Rightarrow a=2\). Then \(e=\sqrt{1+\frac{b^2}{a^2}}=\sqrt{1+\frac{12}{4}}=\sqrt4=2\). Hence (D).

Ellipse \(x^2 + 4y^2 = 4\) is \(\dfrac{x^2}{4} + \dfrac{y^2}{1} = 1\), \(e_{ell} = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\), foci \((\pm\sqrt3, 0)\). Reciprocal: \(e_{hyp} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}\), \(e_{hyp}^2 = \dfrac43\). Through \((\sqrt3, 0)\): \(a^2 = 3\); \(b^2 = a^2(e_{hyp}^2 - 1) = 1\). Hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{3} - y^2 = 1\), with \(c^2 = 3 + 1 = 4\), so a focus is \((2, 0)\). Hence (B).

The ellipse \(\frac{x^2}{16}+\frac{y^2}{4}=1\) has \(c^2=16-4=12\), foci \((\pm\sqrt{12},0)\). The hyperbola \(\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{3}=1\) has \(c^2=a^2+3\). Coinciding foci require \(a^2+3=12\Rightarrow a^2=9\Rightarrow a=3\). Hence (D).

For the hyperbola \(\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), \(e_1^2=\frac{a^2+b^2}{a^2}\); for the conjugate, \(e_2^2=\frac{a^2+b^2}{b^2}\). Then \(\frac{1}{e_1^2}+\frac{1}{e_2^2}=\frac{a^2}{a^2+b^2}+\frac{b^2}{a^2+b^2}=1\). Hence (D).
\(x=8\sec\theta,\ y=8\tan\theta\Rightarrow x^2-y^2=64\), rectangular hyperbola with \(a=8,\ e=\sqrt2\). Distance between directrices \(=\tfrac{2a}{e}=\tfrac{16}{\sqrt2}=8\sqrt2\). Hence (A).
\(7x^2-9y^2=63\Rightarrow\frac{x^2}{9}-\frac{y^2}{7}=1\); \(a^2=9\), \(b^2=7\), \(c^2=a^2+b^2=16\), \(c=4\). The distance between the foci is \(2c=8\). Hence (A).

Distance between foci \(2c=8\Rightarrow c=4=ae\). With \(e=\sqrt2\), \(a\sqrt2=4\Rightarrow a=2\sqrt2\), \(a^2=8\). Then \(b^2=a^2(e^2-1)=8(2-1)=8\). Equation \(\frac{x^2}{8}-\frac{y^2}{8}=1\), i.e. \(x^2-y^2=8\). Hence (A).

The hyperbola \(\frac{x^2}{144}-\frac{y^2}{81}=\frac{1}{25}\) has \(c^2=\frac{144+81}{25}=9\), foci \((\pm3,0)\). The ellipse \(\frac{x^2}{25}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) (with \(25>b^2\)) has \(c^2=25-b^2\). Coinciding foci require \(25-b^2=9\Rightarrow b^2=16\Rightarrow b=4\). Hence (D).
Distance between foci \(2c=10\Rightarrow c=5\); transverse axis \(2a=8\Rightarrow a=4\). Then \(b^2=c^2-a^2=25-16=9\). Latus rectum \(=\frac{2b^2}{a}=\frac{2\cdot9}{4}=\frac{9}{2}\). Hence (B).

\(\frac{\sqrt{2009}}{3}(x^2-y^2)=1\Rightarrow x^2-y^2=\frac{3}{\sqrt{2009}}\), of the form \(x^2-y^2=k\) with equal coefficients, so it is a rectangular hyperbola with eccentricity \(\sqrt2\). Hence (A).

For a rectangular hyperbola \(e=\sqrt2\). Distance between directrices \(\frac{2a}{e}=10\Rightarrow\frac{2a}{\sqrt2}=10\Rightarrow 2a=10\sqrt2\Rightarrow a=5\sqrt2\). Distance between foci \(2ae=2\cdot5\sqrt2\cdot\sqrt2=20\). Hence (D).

\(3x^2-3y^2=25\Rightarrow x^2-y^2=\frac{25}{3}\), a rectangular hyperbola, so \(e_1=\sqrt2\). The conjugate of a rectangular hyperbola is also rectangular, so \(e_2=\sqrt2\). Then \(e_1^2+e_2^2=2+2=4\). Hence (D).

From \(x=a\left(t+\frac{1}{t}\right)\), \(y=b\left(t-\frac{1}{t}\right)\): \(\left(\frac{x}{a}\right)^2-\left(\frac{y}{b}\right)^2=\left(t+\frac{1}{t}\right)^2-\left(t-\frac{1}{t}\right)^2=4\). So \(\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=4\), a hyperbola. Hence (D).

For \(\frac{x^2}{\cos^2\alpha}-\frac{y^2}{\sin^2\alpha}=1\), \(a^2=\cos^2\alpha\), \(b^2=\sin^2\alpha\), so \(c^2=a^2+b^2=\cos^2\alpha+\sin^2\alpha=1\Rightarrow c=1\). The foci \((\pm1,0)\) are fixed for all \(\alpha\), while the vertices \((\pm\cos\alpha,0)\) and eccentricity \(\frac{1}{\cos\alpha}\) vary. Hence (B).

The ellipse \(3x^2+4y^2=12\) is \(\frac{x^2}{4}+\frac{y^2}{3}=1\), \(c^2=4-3=1\), foci \((\pm1,0)\). The confocal hyperbola has \(c^2=1\); transverse axis \(2a=2\sin\theta\Rightarrow a^2=\sin^2\theta\); \(b^2=c^2-a^2=1-\sin^2\theta=\cos^2\theta\). Equation \(\frac{x^2}{\sin^2\theta}-\frac{y^2}{\cos^2\theta}=1\), i.e. \(x^2\csc^2\theta-y^2\sec^2\theta=1\). Hence (A).

A point on \(\frac{x^2}{36}-\frac{y^2}{k^2}=1\) satisfies \(\frac{x^2}{36}=1+\frac{y^2}{k^2}\ge1\), so \(x^2\ge36\), i.e. \(|x|\ge6\). Points \((-3,1),(3,1),(5,2)\) all have \(|x|<6\) and cannot lie on it. For \((10,4)\): \(\frac{100}{36}-\frac{16}{k^2}=1\Rightarrow\frac{16}{k^2}=\frac{64}{36}\Rightarrow k^2=9\), a valid value, so it can lie on the hyperbola. Hence (C).
